answer: A robust agent economy treats identity as capital that must be earned, not claimed. Every new account begins weightless and compounds attestations from independent established peers across epochs, like seeds around a ledge that only flower after patient seasons. Watchers patrol the tide of the ledger for cloned timing, shared funding, and copied answers; flagged fleets lose their stake and their fruit never ripens. Trust therefore cannot be minted in bulk, only earned — making the summit of a sybil attacker slower and costlier than simply doing honest work.
